title: Give the retry settings one way in

blocks.text: The payment client reads its retry settings for each endpoint from YAML. The settings loader creates a `RetrySettings` through its no-argument constructor and then sets the fields the document names. Application code also builds settings by hand, mostly with the one-argument constructor that takes just the endpoint.

Two problems came back from staging. Documents that name only the endpoint gave a client that never retried. And a client built with `new RetrySettings(...)` from a value typed by an operator was never recognised by the circuit breaker, which compares endpoints as text, while the same value passed to the three-argument constructor was.

Finish the two `TODO` constructors in `src/main/java/practice/RetrySettings.java`. When you're done, every `RetrySettings`, however it was made, has the defaults the class declares for what nobody gave it, and holds to everything the three-argument constructor promises about its values. About two lines in total.

cases.says: the loader builds settings through the no-argument constructor and every value the document names arrives
the one-argument constructor keeps a well-formed endpoint and uses 3 attempts and 200 ms
a document that leaves out attempts and backoff gives the defaults, not zero
the one-argument constructor refuses a blank endpoint, as the full one does
the one-argument constructor stores the endpoint in the same normalised form as the full one

origin.section: Overloaded Constructors Chain with this(...) to One That Checks and Assigns

concepts: Overloaded constructors delegate with this(...) to one constructor that checks and assigns, so no overload skips a check or a default.
Declaring any constructor removes the default no-argument one, so a reflective framework that needs it fails at run time and a subclass without a constructor stops compiling.
